report: Read all 16 verses end to end, including the six added units the lemma table cannot see. No construction is analysed two ways: every candidate group is the ASV rendering one morpheme differently (thy/thine, in/of/on/through/with for בְּ, for/unto for לְ, Jehovah with or without a vocative O or a construct of), and each difference is licensed by the printed English.

Supplied subject pronouns are handled consistently across the chapter: a finite verb takes its own pronoun (v4, v9, v12, v13b, v14), a written name earlier in the verse takes the resuming pronoun (v15 Jehovah ... He, rule 25), and a participial verbless clause with no earlier nominal leaves the pronoun added (v13a, rules 20/25). The expletive It of v1 and the cleft It is of v7 are added on rule 25/20 terms, exactly as the contract's own PRO examples.

v7's second when is given to the temporal בְּ of the infinitive construct as its distributed scope over the waw-consecutive that continues the protasis, with the waw taking only And; the note names the And-when pair on the waw as the competing reading. Defensible under rule 55's scope paragraph and rule 52; the partition differs from the alternative by one token, so it was left as accepted.

Rule 31 heads were checked one by one (ten strings on ten, solemn sound on sound, wild ox on ox, palm tree on palm, old age on old, full of sap on full, evil doers on evil); each note names the competing head, and none is a cross-verse split since each is a different substantive.

BSB disagreements: v2 בַּ unrepresented because rule 41 gives the ASV's every to the article and rule 40 leaves the preposition nothing; v14 paragogic nun and v15 suffixed he are rule 32 conventions. None is an error.

No convention recorded: the seven repeated notes each restate a contract rule (rules 12, 15, 19, 29, 36, 46). No promotion or amendment: the chapter taught nothing the contract does not already say, and the corpus shown does not isolate the v7 construction well enough to widen rule 55's scope list.
